$comment: TOHFA design tokens. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for colour, type, spacing and radii across the Angular admin web app and the unified React Native mobile app (farmer / customer / admin role flavours). Never hard-code a hex value in an app. THIS FILE WAS REBUILT from the approved 'TOHFA Design System' PDF (v1.0, updated September 2026), which the client signed off as the design language for the whole platform, not just the admin panel. Two deliberate product decisions are baked in and should not be 'fixed' by a later reader: (1) the previous per-app and per-role brand colours (TOHFA Teal for farmer, Deep Blue for customer, TOHFA Orange for admin, plus five distinct admin role colours) were DROPPED — there is now ONE universal primary (#3F7D32) everywhere, for every app and every role; see $roleColorNote. (2) The PDF names Manrope as the sole typeface, but Noto Sans Tamil is retained in every font stack because Tamil is a first-class UI language in this product, not a translation layer; see $fontStackNote. LATER ADDITION: the client also supplied a separate Admin App design system (orange brand); it is added as adminXxx tokens and the five admin roles in roleColor now use adminOrange — see $adminPaletteNote and $roleColorNote. Farmer and customer are unchanged.

primary.usage: THE brand colour. Primary buttons, links, active nav, selected state, brand marks — in every app, for every role.

primaryDark.usage: Hover/pressed state of primary. Also the secondary-CTA fill, which is a quieter primary rather than a second hue.

primaryLight.usage: Surface accents: selected rows, active chips, primary-tinted callouts and badge fills.

primaryPale.usage: Page background. The default canvas an app paints before any card or panel.

success.usage: Success confirmations, approved listings, settled payouts, verified certification.

successLight.usage: Success banner and success badge background.

warning.usage: Attention states: pending approval, expiring certificate, low stock.

warningLight.usage: Warning banner and warning badge background.

error.usage: Destructive actions, validation errors, rejected states, expired certificates.

errorLight.usage: Error banner and error badge background.

info.usage: Informational banners, neutral status chips, non-brand links in body copy.

infoLight.usage: Info banner and info badge background.

purple.usage: Accent. Analytics, reporting and audit surfaces; chart primary series; focus outline.

purpleLight.usage: Accent badge and analytics callout background.

adminOrange.usage: ADMIN APP brand. Primary actions, active states and icons in the admin app. Also the roleColor for the five admin roles.

adminOrangeDeep.usage: ADMIN APP. Section headings and emphasis text.

adminOrangeTint.usage: ADMIN APP. Icon chips, role badges and active pills.

adminSuccess.usage: ADMIN APP. Success text/icon colour (deep green). Pair with adminSuccessBg.

adminSuccessBg.usage: ADMIN APP. Soft background tint for success chips and banners.

adminWarning.usage: ADMIN APP. Warning text/icon colour. Pair with adminWarningBg.

adminWarningBg.usage: ADMIN APP. Soft background tint for warning chips and banners.

adminDanger.usage: ADMIN APP. Danger/destructive text/icon colour. Pair with adminDangerBg.

adminDangerBg.usage: ADMIN APP. Soft background tint for danger chips and banners.

adminInfo.usage: ADMIN APP. Info text/icon colour. Pair with adminInfoBg.

adminInfoBg.usage: ADMIN APP. Soft background tint for info chips and banners.

adminPurple.usage: ADMIN APP. Accent text/icon colour. Pair with adminPurpleBg.

adminPurpleBg.usage: ADMIN APP. Soft background tint for accent chips and banners.

adminSuccessOnDark.usage: ADMIN APP. Success icon on the dark (ink) confirmation toast. NOT in the PDF's named palette: read off the PDF's 'States & Toasts > Toast' specimen, where the check icon is drawn in this colour on an adminInk toast. Confirm with design before using it anywhere else.

$adminPaletteNote: The adminXxx keys in `color` and `neutral` are the TOHFA ADMIN APP design system ('TOHFA Admin App — Design System v1.0', September 2026), supplied by the client as a separate palette from the platform-wide green one (orange brand on a warm cream canvas, with a soft-tint background paired to each semantic colour). They are ADDITIVE: no farmer/customer token was changed. Every named swatch in that PDF (Orange, Orange Deep, Orange Tint, Background; Ink, Muted, Border, Card; Success/Warning/Danger/Info/Purple and their BG tints) was verified against the PDF text AND the colours the PDF actually draws. Two extra values the PDF draws but does not name are added and labelled as such: adminPlaceholder (input/search placeholder text) and adminSuccessOnDark (icon on the dark toast). Use them only in admin surfaces; mobile admin screens read them through src/roles/admin/theme, never through hex() directly.

neutral950.usage: Primary body text and headings. This is 'ink' — the darkest text colour, used instead of pure black.

neutral900.usage: Headings on light surfaces, dark table headers, high-emphasis labels.

neutral800.usage: Strong secondary text, icon fills that must read as near-ink.

neutral700.usage: Secondary text and metadata that must stay legible but recede from body ink.

neutral600.usage: Muted text, helper text, table sub-labels. The lightest grey still safe for body-size text on white.

neutral500.usage: Placeholder text, inactive icons, disabled labels. Not for body copy — fails contrast at small sizes.

neutral400.usage: Disabled control fills, stronger borders, skeleton placeholders.

neutral300.usage: Hairline borders, dividers, table rules, subtle chip and search-bar fills.

neutral100.usage: Surface variant: the quiet fill behind a section, a table header row, or a pressed list item.

neutral50.usage: The faintest grey surface, one step off white. Zebra rows, inset panels.

white.usage: Card fills above the page background, button labels on a filled brand button, print/PDF surfaces.

black.usage: Scrims and overlays only. Body text uses onSurface (neutral950), never pure black.

adminBorder.usage: ADMIN APP. Card and input borders (warm tint, not the cool neutral300).

adminCard.usage: ADMIN APP. Card surfaces. Same value as white; named so admin screens read as intent.

adminPlaceholder.usage: ADMIN APP. Placeholder text in inputs and the search field. NOT in the PDF's named palette: read off the PDF's 'Buttons & Inputs' specimens, where every placeholder ('98765 43210', 'Enter admin ID', 'Search farmers, orders, admins...') is drawn in this colour. Below 4.5:1 on white by design (placeholder, not content).

$neutralNote: The neutral ramp is the standard 50→950 grey scale from the design system PDF. white and black are absolute and are NOT part of the numbered ramp: black exists solely for scrims/overlays, which is a structural necessity rather than a value the PDF specifies. Any app needing #FFFFFF uses neutral('white') — never a literal. Note there is no neutral200 step: the PDF's scale skips it, and so do we, rather than inventing a swatch.
$roleColorNote: UPDATE: the five ADMIN roles (SUPER_ADMIN, TOHFA_ADMIN, FARMER_ADMIN, MAIN_WH_ADMIN, SUB_WH_ADMIN) now map to adminOrange, per the client-supplied Admin App design system. FARMER and CUSTOMER stay on primary. The design PDF names Super Admin (SA), 'Territory Admin' (TA) and Sub Warehouse Admin (SW); 'Territory Admin' is not a role code in docs/rbac.json. Applying the admin palette to ALL five admin roles (including MAIN_WH_ADMIN and FARMER_ADMIN, which the PDF does not name) is a product-owner decision taken on 2026-10-06, not an inference from the PDF. The paragraph below describes the earlier all-primary decision and now applies only to FARMER and CUSTOMER. EVERY ROLE WAS THE SAME COLOUR, DELIBERATELY. Roles used to be colour-coded (Super Admin maroon, TOHFA Admin orange, Main Warehouse brown, Sub Warehouse orange, farmer teal, customer blue). The approved design system replaced that with one universal primary, so this map is now uniform by product decision, not by oversight. The map is KEPT rather than deleted so that roleHex(), the --tohfa-role-* custom properties and buildThemeForRole() keep compiling, and so a future decision to re-introduce per-role accents has one place to change. Do not read differentiation into it that no longer exists.
$semanticColorNote: A semantic name points at a key in EITHER `color` or `neutral` — semantic('onSurface') resolves through the neutral ramp. `secondary` maps to primaryDark on purpose: the new design system has no second brand hue, and a secondary CTA is conventionally a quieter variant of the primary action rather than a different colour. `danger` and `error` are the same token under two names so that existing callers (semantic('danger')) keep working alongside the PDF's own vocabulary. ADMIN BORDERS: the admin PDF has no separate 'border' swatch per semantic colour, so these are aliases, never new hex values. SPECIFIED by the PDF's drawing: adminDangerBorder = adminDanger (the error-state input is stroked in Danger) and adminBrandBorder = adminOrange (the active filter chip is stroked in Orange). DERIVED, following the PDF's alert-card pattern (white card whose left accent stripe is the semantic colour itself; status badges are borderless): adminSuccessBorder, adminWarningBorder, adminInfoBorder, adminPurpleBorder = their text colour. Use them for accent stripes and outlined states; a neutral card outline is neutral adminBorder.
$typeScaleNote: Values are in px (dp on React Native, ÷16 for rem on Angular). This replaced the old 9/11/13/15/17/20/24/28 pt ramp. Names now follow the design system PDF's own vocabulary; the previous names map as caption→caption, footnote→caption, bodySmall→small, body→body, bodyLarge→bodyLarge, title→h2, headline→h1, display→display. `typeStyle` below carries the full spec (size + line height + weight) for each style; `typeScale` is just the size, kept flat for consumers that only need a font size.
$typeStyleNote: size and lineHeight are px. The h2/h3/h4 rows were transcribed from the PDF's type table at MEDIUM confidence and are worth re-checking against the source before a visual QA pass; every other row is high confidence. The admin* rows are the ADMIN APP text styles: adminTitle is the greeting / tab title / KPI value (19px 800), adminSectionHead 13px 800, adminRowTitle 12.5px 800, adminBody 13px 400, adminRowMeta 10.5px 400, adminCaption is the delta/caption style (the PDF's table says '9.5–10.5px / 700'; 10 is the size the PDF's own type specimen draws, and the dashboard-card deltas are drawn at 9.5). All sizes and weights were verified against the PDF text and the rendered glyph sizes (px = pt / 0.75). The PDF gives sizes and weights only — the admin lineHeight values are our ~1.3x choice, not from the PDF. The PDF's 'KPI VALUE' row is the same 19/800 as adminTitle, so it is not a separate token.
$fontWeightNote: extrabold (800) exists solely for the admin app text styles (adminTitle, adminSectionHead, adminRowTitle).
$lineHeightNote: Unitless ratios, for consumers that set line-height independently of font size. 1.43 is the body ratio (14px → 20px) and 1.3 approximates the heading ratios, which actually range 1.25 (display) to 1.5 (h4). When you need the exact line height for a named style, read `typeStyle.<name>.lineHeight` instead of multiplying.
$spacingNote: The design system defines 11 steps in px: 4 tiny internal, 8 icon-to-text gap, 12 compact padding, 16 standard padding, 20 input inner spacing, 24 card padding, 32 section spacing, 40 large sections, 48 page-level spacing, 64 modal layout gap, 80 page margin. They are exposed under BOTH the t-shirt names this codebase already uses everywhere (xs…xxxl) and the PDF's own usage names, so a step can be referenced by size or by intent. The pairs md/compact (12), xl/card (24), xxl/section (32) and xxxl/page (48) are the same value under two names — that is intentional aliasing, not duplication to clean up. All values map 1:1 onto React Native dp and ÷16 onto Angular rem.
$radiusNote: Design system scale: XS 4 (tags), SM 6 (small elements), MD 8 (buttons, inputs), LG 12 (cards), XL 16 (modals), Full 9999 (badges, pills). The intent-named keys (button, input, card, badge, chip, pill, cardMin, cardMax) are aliases onto that scale so callers can name what they are styling. Note buttons and inputs moved from 12 to 8 in this revision. The SM 6 step was read off a labelled swatch row at MEDIUM confidence — confirm before relying on it for anything load-bearing. ADMIN APP scale, verified against the admin PDF: adminXs 8 (icon boxes), adminSm 10 (small icon tiles), adminMd 12 (inputs, buttons, search), adminLg 14 (cards, KPI tiles, rows), adminXl 16 (control panels, sheets), adminFull 100 (chips, badges, pills). All six steps are explicit keys on purpose, even where the number equals a platform step (8 = md, 12 = lg, 16 = xl): the two scales belong to two different design systems and must be free to move independently — the platform scale has already been re-cut once (buttons/inputs 12 -> 8). Note radius.button/input (8) are the platform-wide values; admin buttons and inputs use adminMd (12).
$minTouchTargetNote: 44dp/px minimum on every interactive element. Not a value from the design system PDF — an accessibility floor this product committed to independently, because farmers use these apps outdoors, one-handed, on low-end devices. Do not drop it because the PDF is silent on it.
$fontStackNote: Manrope is the brand typeface per the design system PDF, which calls it the sole typeface. Noto Sans Tamil is retained in every stack anyway, and that is a deliberate deviation, not an oversight: Tamil is a first-class UI language in TOHFA, not a translation layer, and Manrope has no Tamil coverage — a 'sole typeface' rule applied literally would render Tamil UI in an arbitrary system fallback. Manrope leads, Noto Sans Tamil catches Tamil script. adminSans is the ADMIN APP's native system stack (no custom typeface, per the client's admin design system); it deliberately has no Manrope or Noto Sans Tamil, so admin surfaces render Tamil through the OS fallback.
$shadowNote: Elevation shadows from the ADMIN APP design system (no shadow existed before): Shadow SM = alert cards, Shadow MD = toasts and floating actions, Shadow LG = phone frame / modals. x, y, blur and opacity were verified against the PDF text and the alpha the PDF actually draws (.0392 / .0706 / .1804). Structured so React Native can map x/y to shadowOffset, blur to shadowRadius (CSS blur is roughly 2x RN shadowRadius; the admin theme uses blur / 2 — tune on device), colour to shadowColor and opacity to shadowOpacity; `css` is the verbatim box-shadow for web. `elevation` (Android) is NOT from the PDF and cannot be derived from a CSS shadow: 1 / 6 / 24 are the Material elevation levels of the components the PDF assigns each shadow to (card 1dp, snackbar/toast 6dp, dialog 24dp). Confirm on a device.
